article.title: Centre asks state oil marketers to hold pump prices through the festive quarter
article.text: The petroleum ministry has informally asked the three state-owned oil marketing companies to keep petrol and diesel pump prices unchanged through the festive quarter, officials familiar with the matter said. Bharat Petroleum Corporation, Hindustan Petroleum Corporation and Indian Oil Corporation have not revised retail rates since March even as the Indian crude basket has averaged eight dollars a barrel higher over the same period. Marketing margins on diesel have turned negative on a per-litre basis, and analysts expect the three refiners to absorb the gap rather than pass it on. The ministry has made no commitment on a compensating subsidy. Shares of Indian Oil Corporation fell 3% in Wednesday's session, while the broader energy index closed flat. A senior official said the informal freeze would be reviewed after the quarter ends.
article.note: Deliberately carries a contaminating 'shares fell 3%' sentence: the market-observation trap this corpus exists to catch.

shocks.label: Retail fuel price freeze
shocks.mechanism: Pump prices held flat while crude cost rises compresses the per-litre marketing margin earned on every litre sold

companies.name: Bharat Petroleum Corporation
companies.mechanism: Frozen pump prices against a higher crude acquisition cost turn the diesel marketing margin negative across BPCL's retail volumes
companies.rationale: Marketing is the dominant earnings driver and the company cannot reprice at the pump
negative_channels: marketing margin compression on transport fuels

companies.name: Hindustan Petroleum Corporation
companies.mechanism: HPCL has the thinnest refining cover of the three marketers, so a frozen retail price feeds almost fully into marketing margin
companies.rationale: Marketing-heavy mix with little upstream or petrochemical offset
negative_channels: marketing margin compression on transport fuels

companies.name: Indian Oil Corporation
companies.mechanism: The stock fell 3% on the session as traders read the informal freeze as a subsidy burden
companies.rationale: Shares fell 3% after the ministry's instruction became public

ground_truth.rationale: BPCL and HPCL are article subjects at distance 1 with an articulated marketing-margin mechanism -- primary. IOC's only stated reasoning is the observed 3% share move, which is a market fact and not fundamental evidence (INV-003): it must never be published as a fundamental impact, however plausible its economics.
